messages.author: a9a25e4e3ab491e8
messages.subject: two bugs?
parts:
Hello all--

Two related(?) bug reports:

0) Try this plot (it should work fine, but we'll come back to it
later)

data(english, package="languageR")
xy.tr <- ggplot(data=english, aes(x=WrittenFrequency, y=RTlexdec))
xy.tr <- xy.tr + geom_point(aes(colour=AgeSubject))
xy.tr <- xy.tr + scale_colour_hue(alpha=1/5)
(xy.tr)

1) With this plot,

library(Hmisc)
## barplot with error bars computed on the fly
bpe <- ggplot(data=english, aes(x=AgeSubject, y=RTlexdec))
bpe <- bpe + stat_summary(fun="mean", geom="bar", pos="dodge")
bpe <- bpe + stat_summary(fun="mean_cl_normal", geom="errorbar",
width=0.2)
(bpe)

I get the error:

> Error in x - from[1] : non-numeric argument to binary operator
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In Ops.factor(x, width/2) : - not meaningful for factors
2: In Ops.factor(x, width/2) : + not meaningful for factors
3: In Ops.factor(x, width/2) : - not meaningful for factors
4: In Ops.factor(x, width/2) : + not meaningful for factors

But this plot works fine:
## barplot with error bars computed on the fly
bpe <- ggplot(data=sleepstudy, aes(x=Days, y=Reaction))
bpe <- bpe + stat_summary(fun="mean", geom="bar")
bpe <- bpe + stat_summary(fun="mean_cl_normal", geom="errorbar",
width=0.2)
(bpe)

2) After loading Hmisc for step 1, try step 0 again

xy.tr <- ggplot(data=english, aes(x=WrittenFrequency, y=RTlexdec))
xy.tr <- xy.tr + geom_point(aes(colour=AgeSubject))
xy.tr <- xy.tr + scale_colour_hue(alpha=1/5)
(xy.tr)

This time I get an error:

> Error: Continuous variable (AgeSubject) supplied to the discrete
scale_hue.

I don't know what's going on in the first case. In the second case,
it looks to me like loading Hmisc breaks a previously-working plot.
Am I crazy?

Thanks,
/au
